## Summary
- Allow edited PR comments to dispatch `/fix-pr` when the edit newly adds that command.
- Suppress repeated edited `/fix-pr` commands by checking the previous edited body for the same route.
- Keep edited `/review` PR comments blocked with a visible explanation and no misleading reaction/label signals.
- Update docs and focused tests for the new route behavior.

## Tests

Closes #437

## Notes

- The PR mostly satisfies the requested policy: newly added edited `/fix-pr` can dispatch, repeated edited `/fix-pr` is suppressed, edited `/review` remains blocked with visible feedback, and docs/tests were updated.
- The main rubric gap is a narrow parsing/idempotency edge case where `/fix-pr` is newly added after another existing explicit command in the same edited comment.

## Findings

- **WARNING:** The edited `/fix-pr` allowance appears to miss comments where the edit newly adds `/fix-pr` after an earlier explicit route. In `.agent/src/context.ts`, `getNewlyAddedEditedCommentCommandRoute` derives `currentRoute` from `extractRequestedRouteDecision(...).route`; in `.agent/src/triage.ts`, that parser returns the first explicit route. So editing a comment from `@sepo-agent /answer ...` to add `Also @sepo-agent /fix-pr` later would likely not dispatch `/fix-pr`, even though the new helper and rubric direction support detecting routes beyond the first command. Add a focused test and use explicit-route presence for the current body as well as the previous body.

## Final Rubric Verdict

PARTIAL

`codex` | `gpt-5.5/xhigh` | `Macmini-runner-3`
@sepo-agent /answer i don't understand --> I thought it's as simple as removing that gate condition?

For the narrow case “old comment had no Sepo mention, edit adds `@sepo-agent /fix-pr`”, yes, removing the `github.event.action != 'edited'` gate would probably work.

But it is too broad/incomplete as the actual policy because we want: edited `/fix-pr` runs **only when that edit newly added `/fix-pr`**, and only once. That means the router needs to compare the current body to `changes.body.from`, not just allow every edited event through.

In this PR, that is why the `fix-pr` job gate became:

[`github.event.action != 'edited' || edited_comment_command_added == 'fix-pr'`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/4518d44348a897319634c357c31952ccef923929/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L1184-L1192)

The review finding is about a narrower bug in the new predicate: [`getNewlyAddedEditedCommentCommandRoute`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/4518d44348a897319634c357c31952ccef923929/.agent/src/context.ts#L88-L110) uses `extractRequestedRouteDecision`, which returns the **first** explicit route. So this edit can be missed:

```md
@sepo-agent /answer explain this

Also @sepo-agent /fix-pr
```

because the current route still parses as `answer`, not `fix-pr`.

So the fix is not just “remove the gate”; it is “allow the gate only when current body has explicit `/fix-pr` and previous body did not.” The PR already has `hasExplicitRequestedRoute` for that; it just needs to use it for the current body too.

## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->
<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis-head: 4518d44348a897319634c357c31952ccef923929 -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
PR #440 addresses issue #437 by allowing edited PR comments to run `/fix-pr` only when the edit newly adds that explicit command. It also suppresses repeated edited `/fix-pr` runs by comparing against the previous body, keeps edited `/review` blocked, and adds a visible explanation for that blocked review path. The PR updates workflow gates, context extraction, tests, and architecture docs. The intended policy is narrower than simply removing the edited-event gate because it needs idempotency.

## Review
Overall, the implementation is close and covers the main workflow safely, with no clear authorization regression. One narrow route parsing edge remains unresolved and is already grounded in both reviewer artifacts and the current PR state.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Edited `/fix-pr` after an earlier route is still ignored | WARNING | `getNewlyAddedEditedCommentCommandRoute` derives the current route from the first explicit command, so editing an existing `@sepo-agent /answer` comment to add `@sepo-agent /fix-pr` later does not dispatch `/fix-pr`. `extract-context` also leaves `requested_route` as that earlier route, so the workflow fix-pr job will not run. |

## Progress
- The simple edited-comment case is implemented: bare mention or non-command comment edited to add `/fix-pr` can dispatch.
- Repeated edited `/fix-pr` requests are suppressed using `changes.body.from`.
- Edited `/review` on PRs now gets a visible block response without misleading eyes/status/dispatch signals.
- Docs and focused tests were added for the implemented behavior.
- Existing inline review comments and review threads are empty; I did not post a new inline comment because the same multi-command issue is already clearly covered in current PR discussion and review artifacts.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Edited `/fix-pr` after an earlier route is still ignored</summary>

**Cause:** [`context.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/4518d44348a897319634c357c31952ccef923929/.agent/src/context.ts#L102) uses `extractRequestedRouteDecision(...).route`, which returns the first explicit route. [`extract-context.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/4518d44348a897319634c357c31952ccef923929/.agent/src/cli/extract-context.ts#L205) uses the same first-route decision for `requested_route`, so a newly appended `/fix-pr` behind an existing `/answer` remains invisible to the fix-pr job gate.

**Candidate solutions:** Detect current-body presence of `/fix-pr` and `/review` with the same explicit-route predicate used for the previous body, then make edited-command routing prefer the newly added edited command when appropriate. Add regression coverage for editing `@sepo-agent /answer ...` to append `Also @sepo-agent /fix-pr`.

**Comments:** Reviewers disagreed on severity: one review considered this consistent with first-route-wins behavior, while Codex and rubrics review flagged it as a policy gap. Given issue #437’s “newly introduced explicit command” policy and the current PR discussion, this synthesis treats it as a scoped warning worth fixing.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
`FIX_PR`: the remaining issue is a concrete, localized branch change with a straightforward regression test.

## Final Verdict
`MINOR_ISSUES`

## Action Items
- [ ] Make edited-command detection and `requested_route` prefer a newly added edited `/fix-pr` when it appears after an earlier explicit route, and add regression coverage for that case.
